lanes.title: war notifications: research and design proposal (docs only)
lanes.brief: Director WA3 (D-080): non-participant observers may see battle results as a side-panel notification opened on click; the Director recommended looking up Civilization VI's notification system (events as hoverable icons at the lower right) as a possible add-on (WA3-D: the design is delegated; presentation only; reads fog-filtered published state; never writes simulation state). WA3-R (READING, flagged): observers are polities that can observe the war under fog; war economics are not granted to observers. This is a research and design lane: no simulation code and no presentation code. An earlier draft of this lane was lost with the old container; start fresh. (1) Research that notification pattern precisely (WebSearch/WebFetch if reachable; otherwise say what comes from knowledge and is unverified): icon stack position and behaviour, hover tooltips, click to focus or open, grouping and stacking, dismissal and auto-expiry, turn-blocking notifications versus informational ones, the notification log or history, filtering options, sounds, and known player criticisms. The lost draft found Firaxis's NotificationPanel.lua and ActionPanel.lua as copied into CQUI mod repositories on raw.githubusercontent.com; re-read them if reachable. Compare briefly with 2-3 other strategy games' alert or event systems for good ideas. Label every claim [CODE] (read in scripts), [SEARCH] (search summary) or [KNOW] (unverified knowledge). Per D-069 the research is reference only: the design must be our own genre-pattern design, and nothing player-facing may name another game. (2) Write a design PROPOSAL at docs/m7-plan/notification-panel-proposal.md (marked PROPOSAL; presentation only; reads only fog-filtered published state per PolityKnowledge; never writes simulation state) covering: notification kinds for every event family now on the development branch, each read from its report: observer battle results (WA3); decision-window significant events (reports/G-time-events-t1.md, proposed list); War Pulse events (reports/G-war-pulse-t2.md); two-action windows (reports/G-action-windows-t3.md); siege events: start, breach, storm, relief, surrender, lifting, the three-turn cap, garrison revolt (reports/H-S.md); war-economy events: arrears, mutiny, refusal to march, desertion, disbandment, insolvency (reports/H-E.md); war outcomes: leader execution and fate, sack, raze, occupy, prisoners, war records (reports/H-W.md); naval and ramming events (reports/H-N.md, H-RAM.md); battle endings including the unratified Standoff (reports/H-TR.md); AI-vs-AI AutoResolver results (reports/H-P.md). For each kind: blocker or informational; who may see it under fog (WA3-R; no war economics for observers); icon; hover and click behaviour; stacking and expiry. Also: how decision windows and notifications relate; accessibility; a performance budget; the data contract (a presentation query over a fog-filtered event log, with a deterministic (time, kind, id) order); a test plan (leak tests: an observer never sees what fog hides; tie-dense ordering of simultaneous notifications; expiry and stacking pins); and how it fits the existing Sim.Ui (grep Sim.Ui and Sim.Ui.Tests for NoticeToast, notices, annals, StateChronicle, HUD, PlayerKnowledge and KnowledgeLeakTests; do not modify Sim.Ui). (3) The lane report prototypes/m7-sprint1/reports/H-U.md: research provenance, the decisions the Director must take, limitations. No build is needed for docs-only changes; run python3 scripts/check-doc-links.py --all and say what ran.
